newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 1996 trade surplus rises 81.3 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 1996 trade surplus rises 81.3 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's December trade surplus was US$2.183 billion, up 69.2 percent from December 1995, bringing the full-year 1996 surplus to US$14.704 billion, itself a 81.3 percent year-on-year rise, officials said on Tuesday.
The following is a table of December trade figures in millions of U.S. dollars:
The finance ministry attributed both the export and import growth in December to improved exports to Hong Kong, the United States and Europe and increasing imports from the United States and Europe.

Exports to Hong Kong jumped 25 percent to $2.79 billion, accounting for 27.1 percent of the island's total exports and surpassing the United States to become Taiwan's top export target, the ministry said in a statement.
Exports to the United States grew 8.3 percent to $2.25 billion.
Japan remained Taiwan's top import source, accounting for $2.22 billion or 27.4 percent of the total, followed by Europe at $1.53 billion and the United States at $1.53 billion.
In December, imports of capital equipment and consumption goods continued to rise, gaining 16.1 and 22.5 percent year-on-year, respectively, the ministry said.
Taiwan's trade surplus with the United States was $730 million, rising 14.2 percent from December 1995.
The December trade surplus with Hong Kong was $2.65 billion, up 27.2 percent from a year earlier.
The surplus with Europe was $20 million, down 73.6 percent from last year.
Taiwan's trade deficit with Japan was down 3.9 percent at $1.13 billion.
